turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi, how are things with you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm going back to college at fifty-five and I haven't written an essay in thirty years.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's exciting. The basics haven't changed much. Have a clear argument, back it up, and keep each paragraph to one idea.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Different question. I've got a free Thursday and three trails in mind, I just can't pick.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Let me get through all the options before you weigh in.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There's the gorge walk, narrow and rocky with waterfalls, about three hours, and you need decent grip.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then the moorland ridge, wide open views the whole way, but no shelter at all if it gets windy.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or the old drovers' road, long and easy, mostly grassy, with a village pub roughly halfway.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, that's all of them, Moshi. Which one grabs you?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: On a free weekday, the gorge will be quiet and the waterfalls make it special. The drovers' road is lovely but easy, so save it for a day when you want a pub lunch more than a challenge.
